claims.text: Thermal treatment of near-equiatomic multimetallic solid-solution nanoparticles can enhance their operational stability in the 773–1173 K catalytic regime.
The starting nanoparticles are crystalline, near-equiatomic solid solutions composed of five or more metals.
Thermal treatment causes grain growth in the nanoparticles.
Thermal treatment anneals defects in the nanoparticles.
Thermal treatment relieves internal stresses in the nanoparticles.
Relief of internal stress and reduction of defect density improve nanoparticle stability relative to untreated nanoparticles.
Thermal treatment may enhance catalytic performance relative to untreated nanoparticles.
The proposed intervention is intended to remain applicable to multielement solid solutions having low noble-metal content.

contradictions.description: Catalytic enhancement is stated only as a potential outcome, but the use of 'or' in the failure rule means that failure to improve catalytic performance would falsify the hypothesis even if stability improved. This makes an optional secondary outcome a required success criterion.
